title: Fix seed_from_product_review_log() re-run crash + stale get_keywords.py comment
source: SEO-AUTONOMY-STATE-MACHINE 2nd independent reviewer (it-0006, review_verdict_2.json), non-blocking follow-up
notes: seed_from_product_review_log() unconditionally replays the full REVIEW_PENDING->HUMAN_CLEARED->AUTONOMOUSLY_ELIGIBLE chain for every CLEARED row; a second call touching an already-AUTONOMOUSLY_ELIGIBLE family raises InvalidTransitionError (AUTONOMOUSLY_ELIGIBLE -> REVIEW_PENDING is illegal). Fix: skip a family already at AUTONOMOUSLY_ELIGIBLE with a matching source_verdict (already-applied, true no-op), and only replay the chain for a genuinely new/changed CLEARED row. Also fix get_keywords.py's now-stale comment (still narrates the pre-rework 'seeds every canonical family... not a new restriction' claim rejected by the first independent reviewer).

Fix find_snapshot_asof direction='after' boundary asymmetry (docstring vs implementation)
source: SEO-TITLE-PILOT-OBSERVATION-MEASURE independent reviewer (it-0009, ACCEPT verdict, non-blocking follow-up)
notes: gsc_history.find_snapshot_asof's docstring says direction='after' returns the snapshot 'on or after' target_date, matching direction='before' (which correctly includes an exact-timestamp match via <=). The real implementation's candidate filter is `(c['date'] <= target_date) == (direction == 'before')`, which for direction='after' resolves to `c['date'] > target_date` (strict greater-than) -- excluding a commit whose timestamp exactly equals target_date, unlike the symmetric 'before' behavior. Did not affect SEO-TITLE-PILOT-OBSERVATION-MEASURE's real output (no target date in that run coincided exactly with a snapshot commit's timestamp) but should be fixed (change to >=, or document the asymmetry as intentional if there's a real reason for it) before SEO-METADATA-OBSERVATION-LOOP (Contract H) reuses this function for real observation windows, where an exact-timestamp collision is more plausible.

title: Fix pytest full-suite collection collision: scripts/pipeline/tests/test_git_identity_guard.py's bare `from conftest import _snapshot_local_git_identity` resolves to the wrong same-named conftest.py
notes: Discovered while validating SEO-TESTS-CI-WIRING's pytest.ini change (it-0010). A bare `pytest` invocation from repo root (picking up pytest.ini's full testpaths: tests scripts/pipeline/tests scripts/seo/tests) aborts collection of the entire 12,000+-test suite: scripts/pipeline/tests/test_git_identity_guard.py does `from conftest import _snapshot_local_git_identity` (a bare, non-package-qualified import), and once both scripts/pipeline/tests/ and scripts/pipeline/tests/content_eval/ are collected in the same run, Python's sys.modules import cache resolves the bare `conftest` name to whichever same-named conftest.py module was imported first -- not necessarily scripts/pipeline/tests/conftest.py, the one that actually defines _snapshot_local_git_identity. Reproduced independently by both the implementing session and an independent reviewer against the OLD pytest.ini testpaths (before scripts/seo/tests was added), confirming this is pre-existing and unrelated to the SEO-TESTS-CI-WIRING change. Worked around (not fixed) by scoping the new .github/workflows/seo-tests.yml CI job to `pytest scripts/seo/tests -q` explicitly rather than a bare `pytest`, so this collision does not block that workflow -- but it still breaks any bare `pytest` invocation from repo root today, including any future CI job or local dev workflow that doesn't know to avoid it. Fix: qualify the import (e.g. `from scripts.pipeline.tests.conftest import _snapshot_local_git_identity`, or a relative import, or move the fixture into a uniquely-named module) so bare-name collection order can no longer cause cross-directory resolution.
source: SEO-TESTS-CI-WIRING independent reviewer (it-0010, ACCEPT verdict, disclosed pre-existing finding), formally seeded on cleanup after being named in commit message and STATUS.md but not yet a ledger row

title: keyword_intent.reset_llm_fallback_budget() is never called by recommend.py's production entry point
notes: keyword_intent.py's reset_llm_fallback_budget() docstring explicitly says 'Call once at the start of a pipeline run' (mirrors get_keywords.py's own circuit-breaker reset pattern), but recommend.py's run_recommendations() -- the sole real production entry point, invoked as `python scripts/seo/pipeline/recommend.py` from scripts/seo/workflows/seo-keyword-refresh.yml -- never calls it. Confirmed by grep: zero production call sites. Harmless in TODAY's real deployment topology (one fresh subprocess per scheduled workflow run means the module-level `_llm_fallback_calls_this_run` counter always starts at 0 anyway), but a latent correctness gap versus the module's own documented per-run contract: if run_recommendations() is ever called twice in one process (a future orchestrator, a persistent worker, or repeated direct-import batch/test usage), the cap silently degrades from 'per run' to 'per process lifetime' with no warning. Fix: call `keyword_intent.reset_llm_fallback_budget()` at the top of `run_recommendations()`, and add a regression test proving two calls to run_recommendations() in one process each get a fresh budget.

title: schema_a_refresh's rolling-baseline anomaly check is permanently inert -- nothing ever calls record_run() for that mechanism
notes: SEO-CHANGE-BUDGET-GUARD's independent reviewer (it-0030, ACCEPT verdict) found: Gate 5 (check_merge_safety.py) deliberately never calls change_budget.record_run(family, 'schema_a_refresh', ...) itself (disclosed, intentional -- avoids double-counting a CI rerun of the same candidate diff), and no other production code fills that role yet. Today only the static caps (schema_a_refresh_max_pages_per_run/_max_pages_per_site_per_run) meaningfully gate schema_a_refresh runs; the rolling-baseline anomaly check's warm-up counter for this mechanism will never advance past N=0/3, so it can never actually detect an anomalous run. A related, secondary finding from the same review: Gate 5 never calls change_budget.configure() to redirect HISTORY_PATH, so its reads always hit the real, shared reports/seo/change_budget_history.json regardless of the (fake, git-only) repo_root passed to check_merge_safety.run_checks() in tests -- harmless today only because nothing writes schema_a_refresh keys into that file, but a latent fragility once this gap is closed. Fix: record the real applied volume exactly once per actually-merged PR (not per check_merge_safety.py invocation, which may run more than once against the same diff) -- most likely from a post-merge step in the seo-keyword-refresh.yml workflow itself, or from SEO-EXECUTION-INVARIANTS (Contract J) once it exists, since that card already needs to call change_budget's cross-mechanism counter too. Whichever caller is chosen should also sync change_budget.configure(repo_root=...) the same way apply.py does, for test-isolation parity.

title: page/font Schema A keywords: license.md misrepresents free/MIT products as needing commercial licensing; page has competitor-brand contamination and severe topical genericness

title: Fix pytest full-suite collection collision: scripts/pipeline/tests/test_git_identity_guard.py's bare `from conftest import _snapshot_local_git_identity` resolves to the wrong same-named conftest.py
notes: Discovered while validating SEO-TESTS-CI-WIRING's pytest.ini change (it-0010). A bare `pytest` invocation from repo root (picking up pytest.ini's full testpaths: tests scripts/pipeline/tests scripts/seo/tests) aborts collection of the entire 12,000+-test suite: scripts/pipeline/tests/test_git_identity_guard.py does `from conftest import _snapshot_local_git_identity` (a bare, non-package-qualified import), and once both scripts/pipeline/tests/ and scripts/pipeline/tests/content_eval/ are collected in the same run, Python's sys.modules import cache resolves the bare `conftest` name to whichever same-named conftest.py module was imported first -- not necessarily scripts/pipeline/tests/conftest.py, the one that actually defines _snapshot_local_git_identity. Reproduced independently by both the implementing session and an independent reviewer against the OLD pytest.ini testpaths (before scripts/seo/tests was added), confirming this is pre-existing and unrelated to the SEO-TESTS-CI-WIRING change. Worked around (not fixed) by scoping the new .github/workflows/seo-tests.yml CI job to `pytest scripts/seo/tests -q` explicitly rather than a bare `pytest`, so this collision does not block that workflow -- but it still breaks any bare `pytest` invocation from repo root today, including any future CI job or local dev workflow that doesn't know to avoid it. Fix: qualify the import (e.g. `from scripts.pipeline.tests.conftest import _snapshot_local_git_identity`, or a relative import, or move the fixture into a uniquely-named module) so bare-name collection order can no longer cause cross-directory resolution.
source: SEO-TESTS-CI-WIRING independent reviewer (it-0010, ACCEPT verdict, disclosed pre-existing finding), formally seeded on cleanup after being named in commit message and STATUS.md but not yet a ledger row

title: Fix find_snapshot_asof direction='after' boundary asymmetry (docstring vs implementation)
source: SEO-TITLE-PILOT-OBSERVATION-MEASURE independent reviewer (it-0009, ACCEPT verdict, non-blocking follow-up)
notes: gsc_history.find_snapshot_asof's docstring says direction='after' returns the snapshot 'on or after' target_date, matching direction='before' (which correctly includes an exact-timestamp match via <=). The real implementation's candidate filter is `(c['date'] <= target_date) == (direction == 'before')`, which for direction='after' resolves to `c['date'] > target_date` (strict greater-than) -- excluding a commit whose timestamp exactly equals target_date, unlike the symmetric 'before' behavior. Did not affect SEO-TITLE-PILOT-OBSERVATION-MEASURE's real output (no target date in that run coincided exactly with a snapshot commit's timestamp) but should be fixed (change to >=, or document the asymmetry as intentional if there's a real reason for it) before SEO-METADATA-OBSERVATION-LOOP (Contract H) reuses this function for real observation windows, where an exact-timestamp collision is more plausible.

title: SAFETY-CRITICAL, confirmed live: title_clause_composer.check_grounding_preservation (shared, reused verbatim by description_composer.py per Contract C's own explicit design decision) requires only min(2, len(raw_tokens)) SHARED tokens between composed text and grounding text -- a fixed low floor, not per-entity coverage. Live-reproduced against the mission's flagship target content/reference.aspose.org/en/slides/net/SaveFormat.md (SEO-DESCRIPTION-PILOT-HIGH-IMPRESSION, it-0055): a real LLM candidate enumerating 6 real SaveFormat export formats plus one FABRICATED one ("SVG" -- confirmed absent from all 3873 real claims.json entries and from formats.json's real 20-member SaveFormat enum list, sourced from the actual src/Aspose.Slides.Foss/Export/SaveFormat.cs) PASSED check_grounding_preservation, numerals_trace, forbidden_claims_check.newly_introduced (a denylist backstop with zero real forbidden_claims entries for slides/net -- structurally could not have caught a novel fabrication), and naturalness_evaluator (Stage A passed cleanly on a fluent sentence; Stage B -- the only stage that even sees page claims -- never ran, since recommend.py's real call site never passes placement_count>=2 and Stage A didn't return WARN). The real anchors (the 6 genuine format names) "paid for" the 2-token floor, leaving the 7th, fabricated entity completely unchecked. Independently reviewed and confirmed (fresh adversarial agent, afac85ec18669b0e6): root cause accurate, additional Stage-B-never-runs contributing cause found, blast radius on the already-shipped title pilot assessed as low-but-nonzero (title clauses compose from a single narrow source item, not a multi-item enumeration, and resolve_title_with_composition has zero real callers today -- but the underlying weakness is structurally present there too). Fix must add real per-entity verification for composed text enumerating multiple items from a closed vocabulary (e.g. cross-check each enumerated format-name-shaped token against knowledge/{family}/{platform}/merged/formats.json's real member list when the composed text is a description enumerating formats), not just widen the aggregate token-overlap floor further (a wider floor alone cannot distinguish 'N real + 1 fake' from 'N+1 real'). Out of scope for a content-pilot card to fix directly -- shared infra, wide blast radius across both title and description composition, deserves its own dedicated Contract-level review cycle mirroring how Contract C's own rounds worked. The fabricated candidate itself was caught before any content write and before recommendation_memory served it again (see it-0055 evidence: svg_fabrication_finding.md, and recommendation_memory.json's SaveFormat.md/description entry, outcome flipped to requires_human_review).
